controls.label: Intercept b0
controls.help: Shifts the linear score z up or down; changing z moves the odds exp(z) and the probability p in the same direction.

controls.label: Weight b1
controls.help: Scales the input contribution to the linear score z; a larger magnitude pushes the odds exp(z) and the probability p further from their midpoint values.

controls.label: Input x
controls.help: The feature value; it moves the linear score z, which changes the odds exp(z) and the probability p.

explorations.title: Even odds at a zero score
explorations.instruction: Predict whether p is below, equal to, or above 0.5 when the linear score is zero. Then apply the preset, which sets the intercept b0, the weight b1 and the input x.
explorations.observe: The Linear score z readout shows 0, the Odds exp(z) readout shows 1, and the Probability p readout shows 0.5, the midpoint of the probability range.
explorations.why: With b0 = 0, b1 = 1 and x = 0 the linear score is z = 0, so the odds exp(z) equal 1; dividing those odds by one plus the odds gives p = 1/2, and the probability sits exactly halfway between 0 and 1.

explorations.title: A very negative score still gives a usable probability
explorations.instruction: Predict whether p can become zero or negative when the linear score is strongly negative. Then apply the preset, which sets the intercept b0, the weight b1 and the input x.
explorations.observe: The Linear score z readout shows -6, the Odds exp(z) readout shows about 0.002479, and the Probability p readout shows about 0.002473, which is tiny but still greater than zero.
explorations.why: A negative score makes the odds exp(z) a small positive number; dividing that odds value by one plus itself keeps p close to the odds for small odds yet strictly above 0, so the probability stays inside its allowed range no matter how negative the score becomes.
